text:
incident-bot: Paging: P0 - Hosted SSE disconnect spike for streaming/function-calls. Impact: some customers report truncated tool responses (> 1% error rate). Pager: @alejandra (oncall)

alejandra (oncall): on it. seeing alerts in console. can someone grab quick metrics? CPU/GPU and connection counts?

samir: I can pull connection histogram. running: `curl -s https://ops-api/redwood/metrics?m=conn_hist` -> looks like 5s spike at 2026-03-12T08:07:10Z with many half-open SSE sockets.

henry: logs show SSE heartbeat timeouts then client closed: `ERROR sse: write failed: write tcp ...: i/o timeout` repeated. shipping a snippet below.

henry: ```
2026-03-12T08:07:10.123Z sse_handler.go:243 ERROR conn_id=kj2b2 write failed: write tcp 10.4.3.21:443->52.12.34.56:52312: i/o timeout
2026-03-12T08:07:10.124Z sse_handler.go:187 INFO conn_id=kj2b2 reconnecting client backoff=200ms
2026-03-12T08:07:10.130Z toolcall_parser.go:98 WARN conn_id=kj2b2 tool-call parse error: unexpected EOF
```

alejandra (oncall): ok so disconnects followed by parsing errors. could be client disconnect or server-side stall. cs-ops, any customer reports?

cs-ops: we have 3 inbound tickets from customers A and B describing incomplete tool responses; B reported truncated JSON from tool outputs. They say it started ~08:07Z.

natalie: I'm watching the routing layer. There was a brief control-plane ops deploy at 08:05Z that touched the reverse proxy config for keepalive. tagging as possible. deploy id: deploy-2026-03-12-0805.

samir: pulling kernel dmesg and NIC counters. saw no OOM. but there were many RSTs from some client subnet 52.12.34.0/24 right when errors start.

alejandra (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback proxy change 2) enable graceful socket draining (longer keepalive) 3) route affected customers to dedicated fallback model instance. I'm going to: (a) open a canary routing to fallback (non-proxy-changed path) and (b) ask infra to prepare rollback.

henry: +1 for canary route. adding a temporary tolerant parser flag `TOOL_PARSER_ALLOW_TRUNCATED=1` might reduce customer impact until we fix.

natalie: rollback is queued. infra-ops engineer @lucas is online to trigger if canary doesn't help.

lucas: standing by. I've started rollback plan but waiting for ale's go.

alejandra (oncall): executing canary now: `rb route set --service sse-stream --route canary --to host=stream-c-old --weight=20`

incident-bot: Route change applied: 20% traffic -> stream-c-old at 2026-03-12T08:09:01Z.

samir: metrics update: error-rate dropped from 3.2% -> 1.1% within 45s after canary. connection resets trending down.

henry: enabling tolerant parser flag on one region: `env set TOOL_PARSER_ALLOW_TRUNCATED=1 --region=us-west-2`. applying to 10% pods.

cs-ops: customers A & B see partial recovery; B reports better but some outputs still truncated.

alejandra (oncall): lucas, proceed with full rollback now? we should also capture packet captures for the affected client subnet before rollback.

lucas: starting rollback: `ops deploy rollback deploy-2026-03-12-0805 --env=prod` -> progress 0/3 control-plane nodes rolled back.

henry: parallel task: building timeline. adding to thread: 
- 08:04:55Z control-plane deploy started
- 08:05:12Z deploy reached proxy config push
- 08:07:08Z first SSE write timeout observed
- 08:07:10Z tool parser `unexpected EOF` logged
- 08:09:01Z 20% traffic routed to fallback
- 08:10:20Z error-rate dropped to ~1.1%

samir: NIC counters: massive retransmits from remote subnet 52.12.34.0/24 starting 08:07:05Z. remote client IPs show keepalive failure.

alejandra (oncall): lucas status?

lucas: rollback complete across control-plane at 08:11:00Z. No downtime from rollback itself.

incident-bot: Rollback event: deploy-2026-03-12-0805 reverted at 2026-03-12T08:11:00Z by lucas.

samir: after rollback, error rate stabilized ~0.4%. Most customers report resolution. We'll keep tolerant parser flag on for 1 hour then revert.

cS-ops: Customer B confirms full fix at 08:12Z, they accepted export of logs for their incident.

alejandra (oncall): good. capturing artifacts and assigning RCA threads: hypothesis queue: 1) proxy keepalive change reduced TCP keepalive or introduced aggressive connection resets causing client-side truncation. 2) parser should handle partial frames better; server wrote timeout while client still writing -> toolcall truncated. 3) client-side network issues exacerbated by deploy.

henry: I'll pull detailed sse_handler traces and add correlation ids for affected connections.

samir: I'll upload pcap for 52.12.34.0/24 to the bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1847002468/pcap-08-07.pcap` (zipped).

natalie: I'll review the deploy diff: proxy kept alive options toggled from `keepalive: 75s` to `keepalive: 15s` and `max_idle: 30s` changed, which could cause faster tear-down. adding link to PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/7123

alejandra (oncall): triage decisions: (A) formal RCA will check if revert is sufficient or if parser hardening is needed. (B) action items: rollback confirmed, tolerant parser temporary flag, packet capture uploaded, deploy diff + control plane logs attached. (C) notify product & cs with customer impact summary.

cs-ops: posting summary to customers now. cc @product.

henry: in-thread hypothesis tracker: `H1: proxy keepalive change caused premature connection resets` -> evidence: deploy diff + coincident timing + reduced errors after rollback. `H2: parser fragility` -> evidence: `unexpected EOF` lines, partial recovery with tolerant parser. `H3: client network` -> evidence: RSTs from client subnet; need confirmation from customer's network team.

alejandra (oncall): handing off to samir for deep-dive post-incident. I'm going offline in 15m. please keep updating this thread and open an incidents/rca doc with timeline and evidence. I'll review and sign off on actions tomorrow.

samir: got it. creating rca doc: `/incidents/rca/1847002468-protocol-sse-parse-rca.md` and will link here when done.

incident-bot: Handoff note: oncall change scheduled: alejandro -> samir at 2026-03-12T08:25:00Z.

alejandra (oncall): final notes before handoff: if we see >1% errors again, escalate to oncall-sre and consider emergency rollback of similar config across regions.

lucas: capturing packet captures, logs, and deploy artifacts to the incident bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1847002468/`

henry: next steps for RCA: - dig logs for `conn_id` correlation - instrument server to return partial parse diagnostics in debug mode - add automatic detection for sudden keepalive reduction in deploys (CI lint)

samir: copying timeline and initial evidence into rca doc now. linking: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1847002468-rca (draft).

natalie: I'll add a CI prune rule to flag keepalive changes as risky. opened PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/7130 (draft).

cs-ops: closing customer-facing incident notifications (marked resolved) and offering postmortem once RCA completes.

alejandra (oncall): handing off. thanks everyone.

samir: taking over. I'll continue with packet analysis and reach out to customer network team to validate client RSTs. updating thread with findings.

(End of thread)
